To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sequence of the dihyrofolate reductases of E. coli RT500 and E. coli MB1428 are identical except for four amino acid substitutions.

the amino-acid sequence, including the N-terminus, of the dihydrofolic reductase from E. coli RT500 has been determined, and that this enzyme differs from that of a methotrexateresistant strain by only 14 amino-acid substitutions, all in the N-terminal region.

the amino acid sequence was determined for a trimethoprin-resistant dihydrofolate reduc-tase from Eschericha coli and that this sequence is very similar to the sequence of the dihy-drofolate reductases from other species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the enzyme dihydrofolate-reductase, a key enzyme in the biosynthesis of purines and pyrimidines.
the study of the mechanism of action of dihydrofolate and its reductase, and the effects of the enzyme on the metabolism of the cells.

the development and application of new techniques for the determination of the primary structure of proteins and the application of these techniques to the study of the structure and function of enzymes.

the dihydrofolates reductase from E. coli MB1428 and E. coli RT500 are very closely related proteins, differing by a maximum of four amino acids.
the two enzymes have the same amino acid sequence with the exception of the four residues mentioned above.
the dihydrofolates from these two strains of E. coli differ in only 14 of the 159 residues, and that this difference is sufficient to confer resistance to trimethoprim on the RT500 strain.
